hero.title: Strings
intro.0: Text is a value, not just something you print. You can build it from other values, reshape it, ask it questions, and rewrite it - and each move hands back a new piece of text rather than changing the old one. You write each one and run it.
task.1.title: Build text from parts
task.1.context:
Most text you show a user is **built** - a name here, a number there, glued into one line. Instead of joining pieces with `+`, you can drop each value straight into the text with `$"..."`: inside the quotes, `{name}` and `{legs}` are replaced by those values.

Write a `Critter` whose `Label(string name, int legs)` builds the line `"<name> has <legs> legs"`.
task.1.goal.0: Give `Critter` a `string Label(string name, int legs)` that returns `$"{name} has {legs} legs"`.
task.1.goal.1: `Main` calls `Label("Ant", 6)`, so the output is `Ant has 6 legs`.
task.2.title: Change the case
task.2.context:
Text can be reshaped without changing what it says. Turning every letter to capitals is one such move - handy for a heading, a warning, or matching input where case should not matter. `name.ToUpper()` hands back a new `string` with the same letters in upper case; the original is left untouched.

Write an `Announcer` whose `Shout(string name)` returns the name in capitals.
task.2.goal.0: Give `Announcer` a `string Shout(string name)` that returns `name.ToUpper()`.
task.3.title: Search inside text
task.3.concept: Ask a string a yes/no question
task.3.context:
Often you do not want to change text - you want to **ask** it something. Does this line contain that word? `text.Contains(word)` answers with a `bool`: `true` if the smaller text appears anywhere inside the larger one, `false` if it does not.

Write a `Log` whose `Mentions(string text, string word)` says whether the word appears in the text.
task.3.goal.0: Give `Log` a `bool Mentions(string text, string word)` that returns `text.Contains(word)`.
task.3.goal.1: `Main` calls `Mentions("the cat sat", "cat")`, so the output is `True`.
task.4.title: Swap part of the text
task.4.context:
A transform reads one string and produces a new one with a change applied. Replacing every copy of one word with another is a common one - fixing a typo, masking a name, swapping a placeholder for a real value. `text.Replace(old, new)` returns fresh text with each `old` turned into `new`; the original stays as it was.

Write a `Rewriter` whose `Swap(string text)` replaces every `"cat"` with `"dog"`.
task.4.goal.0: Give `Rewriter` a `string Swap(string text)` that returns `text.Replace("cat", "dog")`.
task.4.goal.1: `Main` calls `Swap("cat food")`, so the output is `dog food`.
task.5.title: What you learned
task.5.concept: Text is a value you can work with
task.5.context: Four everyday moves on text - the ones you reach for whenever you build, reshape, question or rewrite a line.
task.5.summaryIntro: Text is not just something you print - it is a value you can build from parts, reshape, search, and transform. You wrote each move by hand:
task.5.summaryItems.0.title: Build from parts -
task.5.summaryItems.0.text: `$"{name} has {legs} legs"` drops values straight into the text, instead of gluing pieces with `+`.
task.5.summaryItems.1.title: Reshape -
task.5.summaryItems.1.text: `name.ToUpper()` returns new text with the same letters in a different case; the original is untouched.
task.5.summaryItems.2.title: Search -
task.5.summaryItems.2.text: `text.Contains(word)` answers a yes/no question about text with a `bool`.
task.5.summaryItems.3.title: Transform -
task.5.summaryItems.3.text: `text.Replace(old, new)` reads one string and returns a new one with a change applied.
task.5.summaryClose: Each of these returns a value rather than changing the original - the same build, reshape, search and transform moves show up in every language you will meet next.
concept.pr-string-interpolation.def: Dropping values straight into text with $"...", so {name} is replaced by that value.
concept.pr-string-methods.def: Reshaping, searching and transforming text - ToUpper, Contains, Replace - each returning new text and leaving the original unchanged.
